key_insight: Equivariant graph neural networks capture 3D material geometry better than scalar surrogate models, improving optical spectra prediction for materials screening.
engineering_relevance: This can accelerate high-throughput discovery of optoelectronic materials, especially for solar-cell and thin-film optics workflows that need fast estimates of spectra and permittivity.
method: Adapted GotenNet to predict optical spectra from crystal structures.
Evaluated the model on multiple datasets, including a 10,533-structure RPA spectra collection.
Compared against current state-of-the-art surrogate models with emphasis on the 0–8 eV range and static real permittivity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the model outperforms state of the art, with the largest gains on the 0–8 eV spectral window and on static real permittivity predictions.
watch_item: Performance gains depend on high-quality labeled spectra data and careful deployment, since training/evaluation across levels of theory may not transfer equally to new material classes.
paper_title: Equivariant Graph Neural Networks Improve Optical Spectra Prediction for Materials Screening
